neighboring_unit_entries.title: The c=2 Narain partition function factorizes into three completed Eisenstein factors plus triple cusp products
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Repackaging the four moduli as two upper-half-plane variables exposes a special spectral factorization with a regularized Eisenstein constant and parity-matched triple Maass products, explaining why c=2 needs a separate contour analysis.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The c=2 mechanism extends from Narain models to any gapped U(1)2 CFT
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source identifies the minimal ingredients that survive beyond the explicit moduli factorization: subtract the regularized Eisenstein series, use the scalar gap to constrain allowed poles, and evaluate the same nonperturbative correction kernel.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: At c=1 and c=2 extra Λ/Eisenstein poles alter subtraction terms and leading asymptotics, but scalar projection, contour residues at transformed zeta zeros, arithmetic remainder evaluation, and zero-annihilating functionals survive after explicit regularization.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The free-boson and Narain decompositions are special checks; extension to arbitrary U(1)c theories retains abstract theory-dependent coefficients and assumes the stated gap/pole control.
